# `orckit`
- **Version:** 0.0.0-spec

orckit is the process layer for fleets of coding agents that work against
real repositories. The public `orckit` repository is the program. Your
private `orckits` repository is the data: one directory per run.

Most commands act on one run home. The run is resolved in this order:
the `--run` flag, the `ORCKIT_RUN` variable, then the nearest `kit.json`
above the working directory. The private clone is resolved from `--orckits`,
then `ORCKITS_HOME`, then the sibling directory `../orckits` of the orckit
checkout.


- **Usage:** `orckit [FLAGS] [SUBCOMMAND]`

## Global Flags
- **`--orckits <dir>`** — Local clone of the private orckits companion repository.

  Defaults to `ORCKITS_HOME`, then to the directory `../orckits` beside the
  orckit checkout. The same default `create/kit` and `create/kits-repo` use.

  **Environment Variable:** `ORCKITS_HOME`
- **`-r --run <run>`** — The run home a command acts on.

  Accepts an absolute or relative path to a directory that holds `kit.json`,
  or the run name `<owner>/<repo>/<YYYY>-<MM>-<slug>` relative to the
  orckits clone. When absent, the nearest `kit.json` above the working
  directory names the run.

  **Environment Variable:** `ORCKIT_RUN`
- **`--json`** — Machine-readable output, one JSON document on stdout
- **`-q --quiet`** — Print only errors and the primary result
- **`-C --color <when>`** — Color output

  **Choices:** `auto`, `always`, `never`

  **Default:** `auto`

## `orckit kits`

- **Usage:** `orckit kits <SUBCOMMAND>`

The orckits repository is the data half of the kit. It is private.
It holds one directory per run, named <owner>/<repo>/<YYYY>-<MM>-<slug>/.
Run context never leaves it. Only distilled lineage digests do.

## `orckit kits create`

- **Usage:** `orckit kits create [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** modifies state

First-time setup of the private companion repository. Wraps `create/kits-repo`.

Derives <user> from `gh api user`. Creates the repository as private.
Clones it to `--path`. Seeds a short README. Pushes the initial commit.
Refuses to clobber an existing repository or an existing local path.

### Flags
- **`--name <name>`** — Repository name

  **Default:** `orckits`
- **`--path <dir>`** — Local clone destination (default: ../<name> beside the orckit checkout)
- **`-y --yes`** — Skip the confirmation prompt

### Examples

**Create <user>/orckits and clone it as ../orckits**

```
orckit kits create
```

**A second companion under another name**

```
orckit kits create --name orckits-work --path ~/src/orckits-work --yes
```

## `orckit kits ls`

- **Usage:** `orckit kits ls [FLAGS]`
- **Aliases:** `list`
- **Effect:** read-only

Walks the orckits clone for directories that hold a `kit.json`.
Prints one run per line: name, phase from `orchestration/STATE.md`, and
the orckit commit the run descends from. Use `--names` for a bare list
that shell completion consumes.

### Flags
- **`--names`** — Print only run names, one per line
- **`--paths`** — Print absolute paths instead of run names
- **`--repo <owner/repo>`** — Only runs whose target is this repository
- **`--phase <phase>`** — Only runs whose STATE.md phase matches

  **Choices:** `active`, `complete`, `blocked`, `scaffold`

### Examples

**Every run against one target**

```
orckit kits ls --repo acme/widgets
```

## `orckit kits path`

- **Usage:** `orckit kits path`
- **Effect:** read-only

Print the resolved orckits clone path

## `orckit new`

- **Usage:** `orckit new <FLAGS>`
- **Aliases:** `instantiate`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Lifecycle step 1. Wraps `create/kit`.

Copies `kit/` into `<orckits>/<owner>/<repo>/<YYYY>-<MM>-<slug>/`, strips the
`.template` infix, leaves the `skills/` slot as its index alone, and writes
`kit.json` (version 2): the orckit `gitHead` the run descends from, the
digest and dirty bit of every input template, the target repository, the
eval axes, and the lineage digest policy. Offers to commit the run home,
because every event is a commit.

The interview that fills PROBLEM.STATEMENT.md stays with the agent and the
owner. This command does not fill placeholders and does not install skills.

### Flags
- **`--repo <target>`** — Target code repository: <owner>/<repo> (GitHub assumed) or a full git URL
- **`--slug <slug>`** — Run slug, kebab-case lowercase (for example fix-auth-loop)
- **`--directory <path>`** — Subdirectory of the target this run is scoped to (monorepos)
- **`--axes <axes>`** — Eval axes this run is graded on, comma-separated kebab-case
- **`--no-lineage-digests`** — Keep per-input digests out of the public lineage digest
- **`--profile <profile>`** — Template profile (new, not in create/kit yet). Which kit/ files instantiate

  **Choices:** `full`, `issue-sweep`, `toy`
- **`-y --yes`** — Skip all confirmation prompts

### Examples

**Scaffold a run, then interview the owner**

```
orckit new --repo acme/widgets --slug fix-auth-loop
```

**Name the graded axes at birth**

```
orckit new --repo acme/widgets --slug issue-sweep --axes verbatim,evidence,termination --yes
```

## `orckit status`

- **Usage:** `orckit status [FLAGS]`
- **Aliases:** `st`
- **Effect:** read-only

Reads `kit.json` and `orchestration/STATE.md`. Prints the phase, the next
action, the gate table, the deliverables table (PR, Issue, State), the loop
counters, and whether `orchestration/BLOCKED.md` exists. When the ledger
is absent, reports the run as a scaffold and lists the templates that still
carry placeholders.

Exit 0 when the run is active or complete. Exit 3 when BLOCKED.md exists,
so a shell loop can stop on it.

### Flags
- **`--gates`** — Print only the gate table
- **`--deliverables`** — Print only the deliverables table
- **`--placeholders`** — List unresolved <placeholders> in the instantiated templates

### Examples

**One run by name**

```
orckit status --run acme/widgets/2026-01-example
```

**The resume point as data**

```
orckit status --json | jq .next_action
```

## `orckit resume`

- **Usage:** `orckit resume [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** read-only

Sessions are mortal. The procedure is not. This command resolves the run
and prints the pointer prompt that playbooks/codex.md and the run `AGENTS.md`
expect:

    Read <run home>/AGENTS.md and resume this run as supervisor.

With `--launch`, it starts the named host from the run home so that the host
discovers `AGENTS.md`, and passes the pointer as the first prompt. It never
pastes ledger content into the prompt. The ledger is read by the agent, not
by this command.

### Flags
- **`--host <host>`** — Agent host to launch

  **Choices:** `codex`, `claude`
- **`--launch`** — Start the host instead of printing the pointer
- **`--role <role>`** — Which entry in AGENTS.md to resume as

  **Choices:** `supervisor`, `worker`

  **Default:** `supervisor`
- **`--dispatch <dispatch>`** — With --role worker: the dispatch id to point at (for example D-003)
- **`--model <model>`** — Exact model id to pass to the host. An alias is not a pin (RAILS rule 26)

### Examples

**Print the pointer for the run above the working directory**

```
orckit resume
```

**Launch Codex from the run home**

```
orckit resume --host codex --launch --model <exact-model-id>
```

## `orckit ledger`

- **Usage:** `orckit ledger <SUBCOMMAND>`

The ledger is the only memory. These commands read it. None of them
write it. The supervisor writes the ledger, one commit per event. The
layout is kit/LEDGER.template.md.

## `orckit ledger log`

- **Usage:** `orckit ledger log [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** read-only

Prints the last lines of `orchestration/LOG.md`. Each line obeys the
grammar `- <ISO8601> <EVENT> <detail>`. The event vocabulary is fixed:
INVOCATION-ZERO, DISPATCH, RESULT, GATE, DECISION, INCIDENT, USER,
CANCELLED, PREP, ANNOUNCE, NOTE, ENV, BRANCH, PR.

### Flags
- **`-n --lines <n>`** — Number of lines from the end

  **Default:** `20`
- **`-e --event <event>`** — Only lines with this EVENT. Repeatable
- **`-f --follow`** — Keep the file open and print new lines as commits land
- **`--since <iso8601>`** — Only lines at or after this timestamp

### Examples

**Gates and incidents only**

```
orckit ledger log -n 50 --event GATE --event INCIDENT
```

## `orckit ledger state`

- **Usage:** `orckit ledger state [-s --section <section>]`
- **Effect:** read-only

Print orchestration/STATE.md, or one section of it

### Flags
- **`-s --section <section>`** — One section only

  **Choices:** `phase`, `gates`, `loops`, `decisions`, `deliverables`, `stack`, `registry`

### Examples

**The dispatch registry table**

```
orckit ledger state --section registry
```

## `orckit ledger blocked`

- **Usage:** `orckit ledger blocked`
- **Effect:** read-only

BLOCKED.md exists only when a human decision is required. It carries the
exact question. This command prints it and exits 3. When the file is absent
it prints nothing and exits 0.

## `orckit ledger verify`

- **Usage:** `orckit ledger verify`
- **Effect:** read-only

The machine-checkable half of kit/LEDGER.template.md DONE-WHEN:

- every `D-###.md` has at least one `D-###.result.*.md` sibling
- every evidence path in a gate row exists and contains the quoted VERDICT
- every gate-bearing result ends with a `VERDICT:` line as its final line
- every result header hash matches the sha256 of its dispatch bytes
- STATE.md names a next action

Prints each violation as `file: rule`. Exit nonzero on any violation.

## `orckit dispatch`

- **Usage:** `orckit dispatch <SUBCOMMAND>`

The file IS the prompt. A dispatch is written first, then sent by
pointer, so verbatim holds by construction. These commands make the
protocol in kit/dispatches/D-###.md mechanical.

## `orckit dispatch ls`

- **Usage:** `orckit dispatch ls [--ids] [--status <status>]`
- **Effect:** read-only

List dispatches with their result siblings and registry status

### Flags
- **`--ids`** — Print only dispatch ids, one per line
- **`--status <status>`** — Only dispatches with this registry status

  **Choices:** `PLANNED`, `RUNNING`, `DONE`, `CANCELLED`

## `orckit dispatch new`

- **Usage:** `orckit dispatch new <FLAGS> <kind>`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Allocates the next id, writes `orchestration/dispatches/D-###.md` from the
skeleton in kit/dispatches/D-###.md, fills the metadata block, and leaves
the prompt below the scissors for the supervisor. Does not send anything.
Registers the dispatch as PLANNED in STATE.md when `--register` is set.

### Arguments
- **`<kind>`** — Kind and result shortname

  **Choices:** `research`, `review`, `closure`, `build`, `fix`, `verify`

### Flags
- **`--title <title>`** — One-line task
- **`--model <model>`** — Exact model id (RAILS rule 26)
- **`--context-window <tokens>`** — Effective context window, a positive integer of tokens
- **`--reasoning <setting>`** — Host reasoning setting, or not-applicable

  **Default:** `not-applicable`
- **`--transport <transport>`** — How the agent is started

  **Choices:** `native`, `cli`

  **Default:** `native`
- **`--replaces <dispatch>`** — The dispatch this one replaces. Adds the what-changed block
- **`--retro`** — Mark the file RETRO: reconstructed after the fact
- **`--register`** — Add a PLANNED row to the STATE.md dispatch registry

### Examples

**A review dispatch, pinned**

```
orckit dispatch new review --title "Attack the scaffold" --model <exact-model-id> --context-window 200000
```

## `orckit dispatch pointer`

- **Usage:** `orckit dispatch pointer <dispatch>`
- **Effect:** read-only

Prints the three-line pointer that the protocol sends:

    You are subagent D-###. Read <abs path>/orchestration/dispatches/D-###.md
    now. Everything below its scissors marker is your entire assignment.
    Begin at its STEP 0.

The absolute path is for the agent on this machine. It is never written
into a public artifact. Use `orckit ref mint` for that.

### Arguments
- **`<dispatch>`** — Dispatch id, for example D-003

## `orckit dispatch hash`

- **Usage:** `orckit dispatch hash <dispatch>`
- **Effect:** read-only

Print the sha256 of a dispatch file and its first 8 hex characters

### Arguments
- **`<dispatch>`** — Dispatch id, for example D-003

## `orckit dispatch verify`

- **Usage:** `orckit dispatch verify [dispatch]…`
- **Effect:** read-only

A result records the sha256-8 of the dispatch it executed. A mismatch
means the dispatch was edited after dispatch. That is a ledger violation,
not a mystery. Prints each mismatch. Exit nonzero on any.

### Arguments
- **`[dispatch]…`** — Dispatch ids. Default: all

## `orckit check`

- **Usage:** `orckit check <SUBCOMMAND>`

Every rule is tagged by who can check it. The scripts in `checks/` are the
half a machine can check. Each takes its project facts as arguments, exits
nonzero on a violation, and prints the offending evidence on stdout. A check
that fails is a gate failure, not a conversation. These subcommands pass
their arguments straight through to the scripts.

## `orckit check ls`

- **Usage:** `orckit check ls [--names]`
- **Effect:** read-only

List kit checks and the run checks under <run>/checks/

### Flags
- **`--names`** — Print only check names, one per line

## `orckit check porcelain`

- **Usage:** `orckit check porcelain <repo> <baseline>`
- **Effect:** read-only

The main checkout porcelain equals the pinned baseline (RAILS rule 3)

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — The main checkout
- **`<baseline>`** — File with the expected `git status --porcelain` lines

## `orckit check trailer`

- **Usage:** `orckit check trailer <repo> <range>`
- **Effect:** read-only

Every commit in a range ends with the attribution trailer (RAILS rule 13)

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — Repository to inspect
- **`<range>`** — Commit range, for example main..HEAD

## `orckit check footer`

- **Usage:** `orckit check footer <pr>`
- **Effect:** read-only

The PR body carries no AI-attribution footer (RAILS rule 14)

### Arguments
- **`<pr>`** — Pull request number

## `orckit check ownership`

- **Usage:** `orckit check ownership <ARGS>…`
- **Effect:** read-only

The diff against a base is a subset of the dispatch ownership list

### Arguments
- **`<repo>`** — Repository to inspect
- **`<base>`** — Base ref to diff against
- **`<file>…`** — Allowed files, as the dispatch Scope lists them

## `orckit check model`

- **Usage:** `orckit check model [dispatch-dir]`
- **Effect:** read-only

Every numbered dispatch pins a versioned model id and a context window (RAILS rule 26)

### Arguments
- **`[dispatch-dir]`** — Directory of D-*.md files. Default: <run>/orchestration/dispatches

## `orckit check prose`

- **Usage:** `orckit check prose <file>…`
- **Effect:** read-only

Prose obeys the writing rules (RAILS rule 27, playbooks/writing-rules.md)

### Arguments
- **`<file>…`** — Markdown files to lint

## `orckit check run`

- **Usage:** `orckit check run <check> [arg]…`
- **Effect:** read-only

Run a project-shaped check that lives in <run>/checks/

### Arguments
- **`<check>`** — Check name without .sh
- **`[arg]…`** — Arguments the check takes. Everything project-specific is an argument

## `orckit check all`

- **Usage:** `orckit check all [--gate <gate>]`
- **Effect:** read-only

Reads the facts a gate needs from the ledger: the main checkout, the
pinned porcelain baseline, the open PR numbers, the dispatch directory, and
the artifacts RAILS rule 27 binds. Runs each kit check with those facts.
Prints one line per check with PASS or FAIL and the evidence path.

### Flags
- **`--gate <gate>`** — Only the checks a named gate binds, for example G3

## `orckit grade`

- **Usage:** `orckit grade [--counts] [--axes]`
- **Effect:** read-only

Lifecycle step 5. The run ends with `EVALS.md`: a verdict per template,
numbered diff-shaped amendments, honest costs. This command does the half a
machine can do:

- every template the run instantiated has a verdict row with evidence
- at least one verdict is MODIFY or DROP. A kit graded all-KEEP was not graded
- the cost numbers match the ledger: dispatch count, cancelled and replaced
  dispatches, loop counters spent, incidents, inline work by the supervisor
- every axis in `kit.json` `evals.axes` is addressed

With `--counts` it prints the ledger-derived numbers so the author can paste
real counts, not impressions. The judgment half stays with the author.

### Flags
- **`--counts`** — Print the ledger-derived cost of convergence and exit
- **`--axes`** — Print the eval axes from kit.json and whether EVALS.md addresses each

### Examples

**Real numbers for the Cost of convergence section**

```
orckit grade --counts
```

## `orckit lineage`

- **Usage:** `orckit lineage <SUBCOMMAND>`

Every shape in the kit is earned by a run. A digest is the sanitized
EVALS.md of one run, named by slug alone, with no private context and no
absolute path. An amendment PR cites it. No digest, no amendment.

## `orckit lineage digest`

- **Usage:** `orckit lineage digest [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Writes a draft digest in the shape of lineage/evals/YYYY-MM-slug-name.template.md
into the orckit checkout given by `--kit`. Copies the amendments and the
honesty sections. Replaces every private path with a reference handle (see
`orckit ref`), or strikes it when `--no-handles` is set. Includes the
per-input digests from kit.json only when `lineage.includeInputDigests` is
true. The author still reads every line before it is committed. A
sanitizer is a lint, not a reading.

### Flags
- **`--kit <dir>`** — The orckit checkout that receives the digest (default: the one this binary came from)
- **`--staged`** — Mark the digest as staged at the scaffold phase
- **`--no-handles`** — Strike private references instead of replacing them with handles
- **`-o --out <file>`** — Write the draft here instead of lineage/evals/

### Examples

**Stage a digest before the run starts**

```
orckit lineage digest --staged
```

## `orckit lineage verify`

- **Usage:** `orckit lineage verify [--resolve] <file>…`
- **Effect:** read-only

The lineage README rule, as a lint: the digest names the run by slug alone,
and carries no absolute path, no private repository name, no run name of the
form <owner>/<repo>/<YYYY>-<MM>-<slug>, and no raw orckits path. Every
`pkg:orckits/` handle in it resolves when `--resolve` is set and the private
clone is present. Prints each violation as `file:line: rule`.

### Arguments
- **`<file>…`** — Digest files to lint

### Flags
- **`--resolve`** — Also resolve every reference handle against the local orckits clone

## `orckit lineage ls`

- **Usage:** `orckit lineage ls`
- **Effect:** read-only

List the digests in lineage/evals/ and the amendments each one carries

## `orckit upgrade`

- **Usage:** `orckit upgrade [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** modifies state

`kit.json` records the orckit `gitHead` a run descends from, and the digest
of every input template at birth. This command does a three-way comparison
per input: the template at the recorded `gitHead`, the template at the new
revision, and the instantiated file in the run. A file the run never edited
is replaced. A file the run edited is left alone and reported with the
upstream diff, so the supervisor applies it by hand. `kit.json` records the
new `gitHead` and refreshed digests. The move is one commit in orckits.

Without `--apply` the command only reports. It never touches `orchestration/`,
`ctx/`, `sslop/`, or `skills/`.

### Flags
- **`--to <rev>`** — Orckit revision to move to

  **Default:** `HEAD`
- **`--kit <dir>`** — The orckit checkout to read templates from
- **`--input <source>`** — Only this input, by its kit.json source path (for example kit/RAILS.template.md). Repeatable
- **`--apply`** — Write the changes and commit them in orckits. Default is report only
- **`--diff`** — Print the upstream diff for every input the run edited

### Examples

**What changed upstream since this run was born**

```
orckit upgrade --diff
```

**Move the untouched inputs to a tag**

```
orckit upgrade --to v0.2.0 --apply
```

## `orckit ref`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref <SUBCOMMAND>`

A public repository needs to cite a private run note without exposing a
disk path, a repository name, or a run slug. A handle is a keyed digest of
the run name and the file path inside the run. Only an orckits clone that
holds the key maps a handle back to a file. The handle has the shape

    pkg:orckits/<keyid>/<digest>[@<orckits-commit>][?lines=<a>-<b>]

The handle reveals that a private note exists, which orckits key minted it,
and optionally which orckits commit pins it. It never reveals the owner, the
target repository, the slug, the file name, or any path. See doc/CLI.md for
the threat model.

## `orckit ref mint`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref mint [FLAGS] <path>…`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Computes `HMAC-SHA256(key, "<run name>\n<file path>")`, truncated to 128
bits and hex-encoded. Appends the mapping to the private index
`<orckits>/.orckit/refs.jsonl` and commits it, because every event is a
commit. Prints one handle per input path. The index is the fast path for
resolution. It also records which private files have public citations.

### Arguments
- **`<path>…`** — Files inside a run home, as paths or as run-relative paths with --run

### Flags
- **`--format <format>`** — Handle form

  **Choices:** `purl`, `bare`

  **Default:** `purl`
- **`--pin`** — Append @<orckits-commit> so the citation resolves to the bytes at mint time
- **`--lines <range>`** — Append ?lines=<a>-<b>. One range, applied to one path
- **`--content-digest`** — Append ?sha256=<digest> of the file bytes. Off by default. Read the threat model first
- **`--no-keyid`** — Omit the key id. Resolution tries every key in the clone
- **`--no-commit`** — Update the index but do not commit it

### Examples

**Cite a ledger from a public PR body**

```
orckit ref mint --run acme/widgets/2026-01-example orchestration/LOG.md
```

**Pin a finding at a commit and a line range**

```
orckit ref mint --pin --lines 40-58 ./orchestration/dispatches/D-003.result.review.md
```

## `orckit ref resolve`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref resolve [--paths] [--exists] <handle>…`
- **Effect:** read-only

Looks the digest up in the private index. When absent, recomputes the
digest over every file in every run home with every key the clone holds.
Prints `<run name>\t<file path>` plus the pinned commit and line range when
the handle carries them. Exit 4 when no mapping exists on this machine.

### Arguments
- **`<handle>…`** — Handles to resolve

### Flags
- **`--paths`** — Print absolute paths instead of run names
- **`--exists`** — Exit 0 only when every handle resolves. Print nothing

## `orckit ref cat`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref cat [--live] [--all] <handle>`
- **Effect:** read-only

Prints the file contents. A handle with `@<commit>` prints the bytes at
that orckits commit. `--live` prints the working tree instead. A handle with
`?lines=` prints only that range unless `--all` is set.

### Arguments
- **`<handle>`** — Handle to print

### Flags
- **`--live`** — Ignore the pinned commit and print the working tree file
- **`--all`** — Ignore the lines qualifier and print the whole file

## `orckit ref open`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref open [--with <command>] <handle>`
- **Effect:** read-only

Open the file a handle names in $VISUAL or $EDITOR

### Arguments
- **`<handle>`** — Handle to open

### Flags
- **`--with <command>`** — Program to open with (default: $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then the system opener)

## `orckit ref ls`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref ls [--handles] [--run <run>]`
- **Effect:** read-only

List the handles this clone has minted, from the private index

### Flags
- **`--handles`** — Print only handles, one per line
- **`--run <run>`** — Only handles that point into this run

## `orckit ref scan`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref scan [--resolve] <file>…`
- **Effect:** read-only

Reads files meant for a public place: a PR body, a digest, a README.
Reports every `pkg:orckits/` handle and, with `--resolve`, whether this
clone resolves it. Reports every leak: an absolute path, an orckits clone
path, a run name of the form <owner>/<repo>/<YYYY>-<MM>-<slug>, and the
names of run homes this clone knows. Exit nonzero on any leak.

### Arguments
- **`<file>…`** — Files to scan. Use - for stdin

### Flags
- **`--resolve`** — Also check that every handle resolves on this machine

## `orckit ref key`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref key <SUBCOMMAND>`

Keys live in the private orckits clone under `.orckit/keys/<keyid>`, so
every clone of the private repository resolves every handle. The key id is
the first 8 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the key. A new key does not
invalidate old handles. Old keys stay in the directory for resolution.

## `orckit ref key init`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref key init`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Create the first key when none exists

## `orckit ref key rotate`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref key rotate`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Create a new key and make it the default for minting. Old keys stay

## `orckit ref key ls`

- **Usage:** `orckit ref key ls`
- **Effect:** read-only

List key ids and which one mints by default

## `orckit doctor`

- **Usage:** `orckit doctor [--host <host>]`
- **Effect:** read-only

The run `AGENTS.md` says to verify required tools before dispatch. This
command checks for `git`, `gh` (authenticated), `jq`, and `gum`, the ones
mise.toml pins, plus the hosts named in the run (`codex`, `claude`). It
verifies that the orckits clone resolves and is a git repository, and that
a key exists for `orckit ref`. One line per item, PASS or FAIL.

### Flags
- **`--host <host>`** — Also verify that this agent host is on PATH. Repeatable

  **Choices:** `codex`, `claude`

## `orckit completion`

- **Usage:** `orckit completion <shell>`
- **Effect:** read-only

Thin wrapper over `usage generate completion <shell> orckit`. The script
calls back into `usage complete-word` with this spec, so dynamic candidates
(run names, handles, check names) come from the live orckits clone.

### Arguments
- **`<shell>`** — Shell to generate for

  **Choices:** `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `nu`, `powershell`

### Examples

**Install zsh completions**

```
orckit completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_orckit
```
